en: Last season I got fifty maunds of rice. This season, thirty.
This land was my father's and grandfather's. This soil has fed us.
But the same land doesn't give rice like it used to.
The shoots are drying up. I can't even explain what's wrong.
Brother, take this one. Everyone's taking it this year.
I used potash. It worked for me.
Just use this!
Father always used this.
Everyone says something different. Whose word do I take?
The upazila agriculture office? Getting there takes all day.
You don't have to go to a bank to send money any more...
Farming advice is the same now: on the phone in your hand.
Urbora.
Press a few buttons. Urbora asks the questions itself.
Then the answer comes by SMS: what's wrong, which medicine, and exactly how much for your land.
Oh, stem borer? Then take this. This much is all you need.
The warning came before the rain. The urea was saved.
It doesn't make things up. The numbers come from tested code. If it doesn't know, it says so.
Smartphone or button phone. Day or night.
Well... now I understand.
The soil is our gift. The knowledge to care for it is now in everyone's hands. Urbora. May your dreams bear fruit.
